problem: The conversion factors are incomplete and misleading. A length mismatch (cm against mm) changes x̄ by 10, an area mismatch (cm² against mm²) by 100, and a volume mismatch (cm³ against mm³) by 1000. Saying 'a factor of 10 or 1000' skips the factor 100, which is exactly the one a student meets when S is recorded in cm² and L in mm.
fix: Keep all lengths in the same unit. If S is in cm² and L in mm, x̄ comes out 100 times too small; if V is in cm³ and A in mm², x̄ comes out 1000 times too small; a plain length mismatch (cm against mm) gives a factor of 10.

problem: 'both the outer surface area and the enclosed volume' suggests only the outward-facing half of the torus surface is being found. The theorem gives the whole surface of the ring, inner and outer together.
fix: The centroid path radius R = 200 mm gives both the total surface area of the ring and the volume of material it encloses.
